ideas.pitch: A predictive dashboard for campus safety and infrastructure failure forecasting using Poisson regression and historical university incident reports.
ideas.title: Campus Incident AI Forecaster
ideas.why_it_could_win: Follows the exact blueprint of the Apart Research AI Forecasting Hackathon winner by leveraging rigorous statistical modeling rather than a generic LLM wrapper, appealing to judges looking for hard data science.

ideas.pitch: An automated risk-scoring and transaction fraud detection platform tailored for local student-run businesses and campus vendors, using graph intelligence and LightGBM.
ideas.title: Amherst Local Merchant AML & Risk Graph
ideas.why_it_could_win: Mimics the architecture of the DIGITIMES AI Innovation Hackathon winner by combining graph intelligence with explainable machine learning for financial compliance.

ideas.pitch: A no-code strategy builder and copy-trading platform for decentralized perpetuals, allowing students to visually compose, backtest, and execute trading algorithms.
ideas.title: Perpetual Campus Trading Strategy Builder
ideas.why_it_could_win: Replicates the winning formula of the Pacifica Hackathon by delivering a polished, productized no-code creation interface with real execution capabilities within the weekend timeframe.

ideas.pitch: An autonomous multi-agent marketplace enabling students to post errands, have AI agents coordinate fulfillment, and settle transactions securely using USDC escrow on Base.
ideas.title: Autonomous Campus Errands Agent & Escrow
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the proven winning combination from the Synthesis Hackathon by integrating autonomous agent workflows with real-world escrow rails on a fast layer-2 network.

ideas.pitch: A personalized nutrition and meal recommendation platform integrated directly with UMass Dining menus to optimize student dietary goals and wellness tracking.
ideas.title: UMass Dining AI Nutrition & Wellness Assistant
ideas.why_it_could_win: Mirrors the success of the Hour Hackathon winner by solving a hyper-local, highly relatable problem for attendees with immediate utility and a polished consumer interface.
